Woah. Can we please not do that. openbmc/u-boot is a fork of ASPEED's u-boot fork.

Please send support for your SoC to upstream u-boot.

Setting aside historical concerns, here's the _current_ project policy for the kernel and u-boot:

https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/kernel-development.md

Good to know that OpenBMC aligns the development policy between kernel and u-boot
Does that mean OpenBMC will upgrade u-boot to a newer version from current 2019.04?

We will upstream the change in u-boot for our SoC eventually, but we are not doing it yet
For now, we only have 2019.04 u-boot in Axiado Github
We will have another 2025.04 u-boot for our SoC afterward

Could we use this 2025.04 u-boot for this PR if OpenBMC community has concern about this version of u-boot?

> Does that mean OpenBMC will upgrade u-boot to a newer version from current 2019.04?



I think the key thing here is that the configurations for the AST2400, AST2500 and AST2600 SoCs consume openbmc/u-boot's 2019.04 branch because it contains ASPEED-specific changes. However, there's no reason for the bootloader for _other_ SoCs to consume the same branch. We just need the support for your SoC upstream. The bitbake configuration for your SoC can then point to either upstream directly, or a backport of the patches into a branch (possibly master) of openbmc/u-boot.

As such there's no intent that there's an "OpenBMC u-boot". The notion is too broad and counter to the project's needs.
> We will upstream the change in u-boot for our SoC eventually, but we are not doing it yet


Integration into OpenBMC happens no faster than the process of upstreaming your changes. OpenBMC needs this alignment with its upstreams to stay healthy.

> Could we use this 2025.04 u-boot for this PR if OpenBMC community has concern about this version of u-boot?

Please get your changes on the upstream lists, and we can backport them if there's no significant feedback. We are trying to escape mistakes of the past with how the ASPEED SoC support was handled.
